title: Container Bookings: Amount of the Customer Roll Fee
content:
This page states how the amount of a Container Bookings customer roll fee is formed.

## Rule

For every roll still owing a fee, one entry is written, coded as a customer roll fee and of the amendment kind "customer-requested vessel change". Its amount is the product's per-container customer roll fee multiplied by the containers counted for the fee. The full product of that multiplication is rounded to two decimal places only once, at the end. When no roll is still owing a fee, the amount is zero and no entry is written.

## Worked examples (hypothetical rates)

- An invented rate of 95.00 per container on 4 counted containers gives one entry of 380.00.
- Two rolls still owing on the same booking, at the same invented rate and count, give two entries of 380.00 each, not one entry of 760.00.
- An invented rate of 0.00 gives 0.00, and nothing is entered.

The rates above are illustrative and belong to no product.

## Points of judgement

- **Rounding moment:** the per-container rate is never rounded separately; only the final amount is.
- **One entry per roll:** the number of entries equals the number of rolls still owing a fee.
